title: Activities Coordinator - Care Home
description:

As an Activities Coordinator at a Barchester care home, you'll help to create a stimulating environment that enables us to deliver exceptional all-round care and support for our residents. Our ethos is all about celebrating life, so you'll help to devise imaginative, fun and motivational activities that suit every interest and ability. An extremely rewarding role, part of your time as an Activities Coordinator will be spent getting to know our residents and their families before you create tailored activities programmes focused on maximising everyone's wellbeing, independence and social engagement.

ABOUT YOU
You'll need to be warm, empathetic and personable to join us as an Activities Coordinator. Your organisational skills and driven mind-set mean you always get things done and make things happen. Meanwhile, your infectious enthusiasm and creative approach will inspire our residents and staff to get involved in activities both within the home and in the local community. Any similar experience would be ideal, but it isn't essential especially because we'll make sure you have the training you need to develop your skills and progress your career with us.

Free training and development for all roles
Access to wellbeing and support tools
A range of retail discounts and savings
Unlimited referrals with our Refer a Friend' bonus scheme
Employee of the Month' rewards and Long Service Awards'

Workplace Pension scheme, with Employer contributions from 3%

And so much more!

If you'd like to use your planning and people skills in an organisation that provides the quality care you'd expect for your loved ones, this is a rewarding place to be.

title: School Administrator
description:
Job Title: School Administrator
Responsible to: Headteacher / School Business Manager
Salary Grade: 92 - 100 a day
Hours: School ter times
Contract: Temporary

1. Job Purpose

To provide an efficient, professional and effective administrative service, supporting the day-to-day operation of the school. The postholder will support the Headteacher, staff, pupils, parents/carers and governors, contributing to the school's vision, values and commitment to improving learner outcomes, wellbeing and inclusion.

The role will support Welsh Government education priorities, including the Curriculum for Wales, safeguarding, Additional Learning Needs (ALN), equality and inclusion, and the promotion of Welsh language and culture.

2. Key Duties and Responsibilities

The School Administrator will:
- Provide a welcoming, professional first point of contact for parents/carers, pupils, visitors, staff and external agencies.
- Manage telephone calls, emails, correspondence and general enquiries, ensuring information is communicated accurately and promptly.
- Provide administrative support to the Headteacher, senior leadership team, teaching staff and governors.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date pupil records, staff information and school management information systems.
- Support pupil admissions, transfers, leavers and transition arrangements.
- Record and monitor pupil attendance, follow up unexplained absences and produce attendance reports.
- Prepare letters, newsletters, reports, presentations, meeting papers and other school documentation.
- Organise meetings, appointments, school events, trips and visits.
- Support financial administration, including processing orders, invoices, payments and purchase requisitions in accordance with school procedures.
- Maintain effective filing, record-keeping and document management systems, ensuring information is stored securely.

3. Person Specification

Essential:
- Good standard of general education, including English and Mathematics, or equivalent experience.
- Experience in an administrative or customer-facing role.
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office.
- Excellent organisational, communication and time-management skills.
- Ability to maintain accurate records and handle confidential information.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Desirable:
- Previous experience working within a school or educational setting.
- Knowledge of school management information systems.
- Experience of attendance and financial administration.

4. Welsh Government Framework and Professional Expectations

The postholder is expected to demonstrate professional behaviours that support the school's wider educational priorities, particularly:
- Collaboration: Working effectively with colleagues, families and external partners.
- Professional Learning: Engaging in training, reflection and continuous development.
- Innovation: Identifying opportunities to improve administrative systems and processes.
- Leadership: Demonstrating initiative, accountability and professionalism within the role.
- Pedagogy and learner-centred practice: Supporting an effective school environment in which all learners can thrive.

5. Safeguarding

The school is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. All staff are expected to share this commitment and undertake appropriate safeguarding training. Appointment will be subject to satisfactory pre-employment checks, including an appropriate DBS check.

title: Administrator - Temp
description:
Administrator (Temporary)

Location: Newport, South Wales, NP10.
Salary: £27,709 per annum.
Working Hours: 37 hours per week, Monday Friday, 8:30am 4:30pm (30-minute unpaid lunch break).
Annual Leave: 25 days plus 8 bank holidays.
Working Pattern: Office-based.

The Opportunity

Hawk 3 Talent Solutions is recruiting on behalf of its client for an organised, proactive and detail-focused Administrator to join its Operations Contract Services team on a temporary basis in Newport.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced administrator who enjoys working with information, coordinating activity and ensuring outstanding tasks are progressed efficiently. You will play an important role in reviewing outstanding quotations, work requests and associated documentation, bringing together information from different sources to establish current positions, identify missing details and support the timely progression of work.

Key Responsibilities
- Review outstanding quotations, work requests and associated records, bringing together information from emails, spreadsheets, business systems and supporting documentation.
- Establish the current status of outstanding items, identifying missing information, discrepancies, dependencies and actions required to progress work.
- Create and maintain accurate trackers, schedules and action logs to monitor outstanding activity and support effective workload prioritisation.
- Follow up outstanding actions with colleagues, suppliers and other stakeholders, ensuring delays, risks or unresolved issues are highlighted appropriately.
- Liaise with site contacts, customers and internal colleagues to confirm requirements, access arrangements, availability and other information needed to progress work.
- Provide clear and professional updates via email and telephone, ensuring commitments, changes and agreed next steps are accurately recorded.
- Coordinate appointments, diaries and provisional work schedules, supporting effective communication between operational teams, sites and suppliers.
- Input, review and update information within relevant business systems, ensuring records are accurate, complete and maintained appropriately.
- Maintain electronic filing systems and document control arrangements, ensuring quotations, approvals, correspondence and supporting information can be easily retrieved.
- Prepare correspondence, schedules, reports, meeting notes and other administrative documentation using Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook.
- Monitor shared mailboxes and allocated enquiries, ensuring correspondence is directed appropriately and outstanding actions are not overlooked.
- Support operational meetings and reviews by preparing relevant information, recording actions and following up agreed next steps.
- Identify opportunities to improve administrative processes, information management and the overall efficiency of the Contract Services function.
- Work independently to manage day-to-day responsibilities while providing effective support to the Operations Manager and wider team.

Experience Required
- Previous experience in an administration, coordination or business support role.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word and Outlook.
- Experience maintaining spreadsheets, trackers, schedules, action logs or similar records.
- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage a varied workload, prioritise competing demands and meet deadlines.
- Excellent attention to detail, particularly when reviewing information, maintaining records and identifying discrepancies.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to liaise professionally with customers, suppliers, site contacts and internal colleagues.
- A flexible and adaptable approach, with a willingness to support the wider operational team.
- Experience within property, facilities management, construction, maintenance, local authority or a similar operational environment would be advantageous.
- Previous exposure to quotations, work orders, purchasing or contract administration processes would be beneficial.
- A good standard of general education, including English and Maths, or equivalent demonstrable experience.
- A UK driving licence would be advantageous due to occasional travel to other offices or sites.

title: Quality Administrator
description:
Administrators - Why You Should Apply

A new career, no degree needed: You don't need a lab or science background to become a QC Administrator here. Everything is fully trained, so if you've got sharp admin skills and an eye for detail, this is your way into the science sector without going back to university.

Build your day around you: Flexitime lets you start any time between 7:30am and 9:30am and finish between 3:30pm and 5:30pm. Do the school run, beat the traffic, or get to the gym while it's quiet, then shape your hours around your life.

Grow with a busy lab: New business is coming in fast, and the small team is set to expand, so you're joining at the point where there's real room to move up.

Your salary, benefits & hours of work
- 27,000 and annual bonus
- Flexitime: start any time between 7:30am and 9:30am, finish between 3:30pm and 5:30pm
- Monday to Friday, no weekends
- Full training from day one
- No weekend or bank holiday working, with a shutdown from Christmas to the New Year.
- Holidays 24 days plus 8 Bank Holidays (increasing with length of service - one extra day for every 5 years to a maximum of 25 years)

What you'll do as the Quality Control Administrator

You'll keep the Quality Control project team running smoothly, handling the admin that gets samples tested and results back to customers.
- Book stability and project samples into the QC systems
- Organise despatch of samples to partner testing laboratories, raising purchase orders and labelling correctly
- Collect and trend data, create Certificates of Analysis and draft customer quotes
- Complete and archive records, keeping the lab audit-ready
- Prepare reagents and run basic sample checks once trained
- Order consumables and support improvements across the lab

What you'll need to apply for the Quality Administrator
- Strong, hands-on administration experience with a genuine eye for detail
- Good computer literacy (Microsoft Office 365) and happy to learn new systems.

title: Finance Assistant
company: Môrwell Talent Solutions Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Finance Assistant

Cwmbran

Salary up to £32,000 DOE

Full-Time

Permanent

Fully Office-Based

Môrwell Talent Solutions is delighted to be supporting a growing and well-established business in the Cwmbran area with the appointment of a Finance Assistant to join its busy finance team.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with previous accounts and purchase ledger experience who is looking to develop their career within a dynamic and supportive business.

The Role

Reporting to the Financial Controller, you will play an important role in supporting the day-to-day running of the finance function, taking responsibility for the purchase ledger and ensuring financial transactions are processed accurately and efficiently.

Working closely with the wider finance team, you will be involved in a variety of accounting and reconciliation activities, helping to maintain accurate financial records and support the smooth operation of the department.

- Processing supplier invoices, expenses and financial transactions using Sage 50.
- Taking responsibility for the purchase ledger function.
- Managing customer self-billing processes and submitting documentation through customer portals.
- Processing supplier stock invoices and maintaining accurate financial records.
- Assisting with monthly account reconciliations.
- Supporting monthly ERP system reconciliations and reporting.
- Investigating and resolving finance-related queries with suppliers and colleagues.
- Providing general finance administration support to the Financial Controller and wider management team.
- Identifying opportunities to improve processes and efficiencies within the finance function.

Skills & Experience
- Previous experience working within an accounts or finance department.
- A minimum of one year's finance-related experience.
- Good understanding of purchase ledger processes.
- Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Good organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
- Confident communication skills and the ability to work effectively as part of a team.

- Salary up to £32,000 doe.

title: Retail Marketing Coordinator
description:
Retail Marketing Coordinator Field-Based

Newport / South Wales 40,000 + Company Car

Monday-Friday 80% Field-Based Fast-Growing Automotive Group

People person? Commercially driven? Love the freedom of being out in the field?

Zachary Daniels is exclusively recruiting for a large, rapidly growing automotive group with a major UK-wide retail presence.

Following a significant acquisition, the business has welcomed numerous additional retail locations into its network and is looking for a confident, proactive Retail Marketing Coordinator to help drive performance across its expanding retail estate.

They need someone who can get out there, meet people, build relationships and ensure their brands are brilliantly represented.

Think less sitting behind a desk, more getting out there and making things happen.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone from field sales, field marketing, account management or retail operations who enjoys variety, travel and the independence to manage their own working week.

The Opportunity:

You'll be the key connection between the central marketing team and retail sites, building relationships, delivering campaigns and spotting opportunities to improve performance.

With approximately 80% of your time spent visiting retail locations, predominantly across the Midlands and South, you'll enjoy genuine autonomy and the opportunity to make a real difference within a growing business.

What You'll Be Doing:
- Being the face of the business: Visiting retail sites, engaging with store teams and Area Managers, and building strong relationships.
- Delivering retail marketing: Coordinating in-store campaigns, promotions, product launches and marketing materials.
- Driving commercial opportunities: Identifying ways to improve sales, brand visibility and customer experience.
- Supporting the retail environment: Overseeing merchandising, signage, fixtures, product displays and range planning.
- Keeping projects on track: Coordinating marketing assets, logistics, suppliers, budgets and deadlines.
- Tracking performance: Reviewing retail activity, competitor trends and store performance to recommend improvements.

Who We're Looking For?

We're interested in energetic, confident and self-sufficient people who love working with others and taking ownership.

You might currently work in field sales, territory management, field marketing, account management, merchandising or multi-site retail operations.

You'll have excellent communication skills, commercial awareness, strong organisation and the confidence to work independently.

You don't need to come from an identical role - attitude, initiative and the ability to build relationships are what really matter.

Location & Package:

Ideally based in Newport, South Wales or surrounding areas, with regular travel across the Midlands and South.

You'll work from a regional office at least one day per week, with the Newport office located at Delta House, Meadows Road, Queensway Meadows Industrial Estate, Newport, NP19 4 SS. Occasional attendance at Newton-le-Willows HQ can be arranged flexibly.
- 40,000 annual salary + company car
- 23 days' holiday plus bank holidays, rising to 24 days from year two
- Monday-Friday, 40-hour working week
- Plenty of autonomy, independence and variety
- The opportunity to join an ambitious, expanding UK-wide automotive group

Ready for Your Next Challenge?

If you're at your best when you're out meeting people, building relationships and making things happen, we'd love to hear from you.

Zachary Daniels is proud to represent this business exclusively. Apply now and take the next step in your career!
